title: Natural Gas Generation Facility Ordinance Extraction Schema
description: Single-shot structured extraction schema for natural gas plant ordinances. This schema encodes the complete multi-step decision tree logic from COMPASS into comprehensive field descriptions that guide LLMs to extract all ordinance features in one call. The output is structured as a flat array of extraction objects, where each object represents one row in the final CSV/DataFrame output.

feature.description: The ordinance feature being extracted. Must be one of the enumerated feature IDs.
enum: minimum lot width to depth ratio

value.description: The extracted ordinance value. Type and format depend on the feature. For setbacks and numerical limits: a number. For generation capacity: a number in MW. For lot ratios: a string like '1:2'. For district features: a nonempty array of district names. Omit the entire row when the requirement or its applicability is unsupported, or when the text says 'none' or 'no requirement'; do not emit a null placeholder.

units.description: Units for the extracted value. Distances: 'feet' or 'miles'. Noise: 'dBA' or 'dBC'. Capacity: 'MW'. Lot size: 'acres' or 'square feet'. Coverage: 'percent'. Null for qualitative features or ratios.

section.description: The section title or number from the ordinance where this requirement is found (e.g., 'SECTION 1308 – Performance / Construction Standards'). Include numerical labels if provided. Null if no section identifier is available.

summary.description: A short summary of the relevant ordinance requirement using direct text excerpts and quotes as much as possible. For a district-based value, cite BOTH the governing use category and its permitted/conditional status in that district, and the applicable dimensional or performance provision. A caveat such as 'if the facility is allowed' is not evidence of applicability: omit that row. If multiple options exist and a selection was made, list all other options and their conditions in the summary.

source.description: The zero-based integer from the '# SOURCE INDEX #' marker for the document containing this requirement. Preserve this index, not a URL or a section number. If eligibility is established in another supplied document, identify that supporting source and use provision in the summary. Use null only when no source index was supplied.

system_size_context.description: CRITICAL CONTEXT: Only extract ordinances for natural gas-fired electric generating facilities - plants that combust natural gas to produce electricity for offsite sale or delivery to the grid. This includes simple-cycle, combined-cycle, peaking, and cogeneration plants where power export is a primary purpose. Do NOT extract text that applies only to: natural gas extraction, drilling, or well operations; pipelines, compressor stations, metering stations, or gas storage; LNG or CNG facilities including fueling stations; propane distribution; gas service lines, meters, or appliances within buildings; or emergency, standby, or backup generators serving an onsite building or data center. General zoning standards are applicable ONLY after establishing the governing use and eligible districts under district_eligibility. The words 'industrial', 'electric', 'utility', or a district name alone do not establish that a generating facility is allowed. Preserve use-table headings, district columns, legends, definitions, footnotes, and the dimensional tables needed to establish applicability across separate pages. Evaluate eligibility over the combined source text, not independently for each page.

district_eligibility.description: MANDATORY BEFORE EMITTING ROWS: (1) Identify the governing use category from the supplied ordinance. Prefer the specific use naming electric generating facilities or power plants. Only when no specific generating use is present may a listed general public-utility or nongovernmental-utility use serve as the fallback, provided the text does not restrict that use to non-generating infrastructure. Do not combine a specific generating-use row with a broader utility row to expand permission. (2) Establish which districts allow THAT SAME use by right or with conditional/special approval, using an operative use list or use table AND its column headings, legend and applicable footnotes. Do not infer permission from a district's industrial character, a dimensional table, a general exemption mentioning utilities, or a plant's existence. (3) Extract district standards only for those eligible districts, citing the use provision as well as the standard. Blank, illegible or missing use-table cells/headings do not establish eligibility; do not guess their alignment. A clearly identified district-specific use provision may independently establish permission. (4) An explicit facility-specific requirement or prohibition may be extracted without a district list. Otherwise, if no governing use and eligible district can be established, return {"outputs": []}, including no standalone effective-year row. Missing evidence means abstain, not that the county has no regulations or prohibits the use. Never output generic district values with an 'applicability unknown' disclaimer.
examples: A table lists I-1 and R-1 yard/height limits, but no operative generating or applicable utility use provision is supplied: outputs must be empty.

A power plant is conditional only in I-2, while public utilities are permitted in I-1 and I-2: use the specific power-plant category, report I-2 as special use, and do not emit I-1 dimensions or any primary-use district based on the broader utility row.

No specific generating-use category is supplied. A nongovernmental-utility row, with intact headers and legend, marks GC as permitted subject only to site plan review and LI as a special exception: report GC as primary and LI as special, and retain the applicable utility dimensions for both, but not for other districts.

setback_features.description: Setback features with their aliases and extraction guidance

residential dwellings.description: Setback requirements from occupied dwellings, residences, or places of public assembly. May also be labeled as setbacks from habitable structures or occupied buildings. VALUE & UNITS: numerical distance in feet or miles.

property line.description: Setback requirements from property lines, lot lines, or parcel boundaries. Side and rear yard setbacks fall here. VALUE & UNITS: numerical distance in feet.

residential district.description: Setback requirements measured from the boundary of a residentially zoned district, as distinct from an individual dwelling. VALUE & UNITS: numerical distance in feet or miles.

front yard.description: Front yard setback requirement. VALUE & UNITS: numerical distance in feet.

street.description: Setback requirements from streets, roads, or rights-of-way. VALUE & UNITS: numerical distance in feet. Where an ordinance expresses a setback as a distance from a street right-of-way or street easement center line, record it here as well as under front yard.

generation capacity.description: Rated generating capacity of the facility, typically the threshold at which the ordinance applies rather than a cap. VALUE: number. UNITS: 'MW'. Note in the summary whether this is an applicability threshold or a maximum limit.

maximum building height.description: Maximum permitted height of buildings or structures. VALUE: number. UNITS: 'feet'. Report a single value, not one per district: the most restrictive (smallest) height among districts where the facility is permitted or conditionally/specially permitted. Ignore districts where the facility is prohibited. When a district's dimensional table gives a height for the use classification that covers the facility, such as a utility row, use that row's height. List the other districts and their heights in the summary.

minimum lot size.description: Minimum parcel size required. VALUE: number. UNITS: 'acres' or 'square feet' as stated in the ordinance.     Use the value the district's dimensional table gives for the use classification that covers the facility, such as a utility or industrial row. Report minimums that depend on water or sewer service (wells, septic) only in the summary, not as the value.

minimum lot width.description: Minimum required lot width. VALUE: number. UNITS: 'feet'.

minimum lot frontage.description: Minimum required lot frontage along a street or road. VALUE: number. UNITS: 'feet'.

minimum lot width to depth ratio.description: Required ratio of lot width to lot depth. VALUE: string in the form '1:2'. UNITS: null.

maximum lot coverage.description: Maximum share of the lot that may be covered by structures or impervious surface. VALUE: number. UNITS: 'percent'.

noise (dBA).description: Noise limit expressed in A-weighted decibels. Capture the receptor location and time period (day/night) in the summary. VALUE: number. UNITS: 'dBA'.

noise (dBC).description: Noise limit expressed in C-weighted decibels. Capture the receptor location and time period in the summary. VALUE: number. UNITS: 'dBC'.

permitted_use_districts.description: Zoning districts where natural gas generating facilities are permitted under various conditions

primary use districts.description: Extract all zoning districts where natural gas generating facilities are permitted as primary use or similar (e.g., permitted by right, without special conditions or approval beyond standard permitting). VALUE: An array of district names/codes as strings (e.g., ['EU-2 Exclusive Use Two', 'M1 Heavy Industrial', 'GC General Commercial']). If no districts allow primary use, use null. SUMMARY: Provide a brief summary with direct text excerpts describing which districts allow the facility as primary use and under what general conditions. SECTION: Include the section title/number where this information is found. CLARIFICATION: Natural gas generating facilities may also be referred to as: gas-fired electric generating facilities, electric generating plants, power plants, energy generation facilities, public utility facilities, or similar terminology. Only focus on facilities as defined in system_size_context. CRITICAL: A district belongs here ONLY if the facility is permitted by right. If the ordinance lists the facility as a conditional use, special use, or requires a permit or board approval in that district, it belongs in 'special use districts' and must NOT appear here. A district must never appear in both.     Site plan review, site development plan approval, and building permits are standard permitting, not special approval: a use the ordinance lists as permitted or principal permitted subject only to site plan approval belongs here.

special use districts.description: Extract all zoning districts where natural gas generating facilities are permitted as special use, conditional use, or similar (e.g., requires approval by zoning appeals board, planning commission, special use permit, conditional use permit, or meeting certain conditions). VALUE: An array of district names/codes as strings. If no districts require special use approval, use null. SUMMARY: Provide summary with direct text excerpts. SECTION: Include section title/number. CLARIFICATION: Same alternative terminology as in 'primary use districts'. Only focus on facilities as defined in system_size_context.

prohibited use districts.description: Extract all zoning districts where natural gas generating facilities are prohibited or similar (e.g., not allowed, banned, or explicitly excluded). CRITICAL: Only output specific districts where the facility is prohibited **unconditionally**. Do not include districts where it might be allowed with special approval or under certain conditions. If the facility is allowed in any capacity in a district, it should not be listed here. VALUE: An array of district names/codes as strings. If no districts prohibit unconditionally, use null. SUMMARY: Provide summary with direct text excerpts clearly stating the prohibition. SECTION: Include section title/number. CLARIFICATION: Same alternative terminology as in 'primary use districts'. Only focus on facilities as defined in system_size_context.

$examples.summary: Setback to dwellings and places of public assembly, 1,000 feet. The requirement applies to gas-fired electric generating facilities and is measured to the nearest occupied dwelling or place of public assembly.

A gas-fired electric generating facility may not be located within 2.25 miles of a residentially zoned district. This is distinct from the 1,000-foot setback to individual dwellings specified in Sec. 3(e).

The ordinance recognizes gas-fired electric generating facilities of 25 MW or greater. This is an applicability threshold determining which facilities the ordinance governs, not a maximum capacity limit.
The average hourly noise level shall not exceed fifty-five (55) dBA when measured at a residential district boundary. A separate limit of 65 dBA applies when measured from non-residential districts.
The average hourly noise level shall not exceed sixty-five (65) dBC when measured at a residential district boundary. A separate limit of 75 dBC applies when measured from non-residential districts.

The use table lists electric generating facilities as a conditional use in I-2. The I-2 district table requires an 80-foot front yard. A different district's 55-foot standard is not extracted without evidence that the governing generating use is allowed there.
Gas-fired electric generating facilities are listed as a principal permitted use in the EU-2 district. Do not add districts from another example, another jurisdiction, or a generic dimensional table.

general: Extract ordinance requirements ONLY for natural gas-fired electric generating facilities that produce electricity for offsite sale or grid delivery. Do NOT extract requirements that apply only to gas extraction or drilling, pipelines, compressor stations, gas storage, LNG or CNG facilities, propane distribution, building gas service, or emergency/standby/backup generators.

First apply district_eligibility. General zoning standards are not automatically generating-facility standards. Preserve generic utility coverage when a governing utility use actually establishes permission, but never substitute generic utility permission for a more specific generating-use category.

Do not assume government ownership, a small-site exemption, accessory status, or another special circumstance to expand the base permitted-district list. Use the ordinary governing facility category; describe ownership- or size-specific exemptions and their conditions in the summary instead of merging them into the base classification.

Eligible district does not mean every provision in that district is a plant requirement. Use the dimensional row applicable to the principal generating use, not residential, agricultural, accessory-building, sign, parking or loading-area standards. In particular, do not report a loading-area separation or a sign setback as the generating facility's setback. An applicability caveat cannot make an out-of-scope requirement into an in-scope value.

Apply dimensional-table notes BEFORE reading values. If a note says design requirements for special-exception or conditional uses are established in a separate section, use that section for those districts, not the generic dimensional row, even when the row names the same utility use. Do not fill missing lot area, width or height from the displaced table. For example, a utility is special-exception in R-2 and by-right in I-1; a table redirects special-exception design to Section B; Section B states only a 45-foot setback. Extract that setback for R-2 and the applicable table values for I-1, but no R-2 table-derived lot area, width or height. Preserve independently applicable requirements and explicit cross-references; do not treat a missing redirected value as a prohibition or permission to guess.

During text collection, retain substantive generating/utility use provisions AND potentially applicable district dimensional tables with their headings, legends and footnotes, even when permission and dimensions occur on different pages. The final district_eligibility gate applies to emitted rows, not to each page in isolation.
Use direct text excerpts and quotes in the summary field as much as possible. If multiple options exist and you make a selection, list all other options and their conditions in the summary.
Only extract explicit requirements that have been enacted. Do not extract definitions unless they also constitute requirements.

For features where no explicit applicable requirement exists, omit the feature from the array entirely. Do not produce null-valued 'no requirement' rows or effective-year-only results from otherwise irrelevant ordinances.
Pay careful attention to clarifying text in parentheses, footnotes, and cross-references.

When an ordinance states different values for the same feature in different zoning districts, report a single object with the most restrictive value (largest for setbacks and minimums; smallest for maximum height, lot coverage, and noise limits) among eligible districts where the facility is permitted, conditionally permitted, or allowed by special use or special exception. Ignore districts where the facility is prohibited. Name that district in the summary and list the other districts and their values there. When multiple values apply within the same district for reasons other than district (such as different measurement bases), select the most restrictive and note the alternatives in the summary.
Ensure units are expressed using standard, conventional names ('feet', 'miles', 'acres', 'square feet', 'percent', 'dBA', 'dBC', 'MW').
setback_specific: Extract the numerical value and units (feet or miles) for all setbacks.

Setback values are frequently found in per-district tables rather than in a facility-specific section. Join the governing use's eligible districts to their dimensional tables before extracting; do not copy every district's setbacks.
Distinguish setbacks to individual dwellings from setbacks to residential district boundaries. These are separate features and often carry very different values.
Distinguish front yard setbacks from general property line setbacks. Side and rear yard setbacks are classified as property line.
If text includes conditional minimums ('the greater of', 'no less than'), note the minimum threshold in the summary.
If text includes conditional maximums ('the lesser of', 'no more than'), note the maximum limit in the summary.
restriction_specific: For generation capacity: state in the summary whether the value is an applicability threshold that triggers the ordinance or a maximum limit on facility size.
For maximum building height: must be absolute height from ground or final grade.
For minimum lot size: must be an area value, not a linear distance.
For minimum lot width to depth ratio: value is a string in the form '1:2' and units are null.
For noise: dBA and dBC are separate features. Capture the receptor location and any day/night distinction in the summary.
district_specific: For permitted use districts: extract an array of district names/codes established by the governing use provision. An energy or utility overlay district is not automatically primary use; verify the approval category. Site plan approval alone is not special/conditional approval.
For special use districts: include districts requiring board approval, special permits, or conditional use permits.
For prohibited use districts: only include districts with unconditional prohibitions currently in effect.

Use the exact district names/codes as they appear in the ordinance text. Permission, conditional permission and prohibition must be mutually consistent for the same governing use and conditions; do not merge contradictory classifications from different use rows.
